text:
elaine_sales: Quick presales ticket from EU bank for a 4-week POC. They want: (A) an explicit EU data residency statement for the POC, (B) a single-page data flow diagram they can hand to their vendor risk team, and (C) a short note on how Dedicated vs Private vs Hosted affects price. Need a reply to the customer tomorrow morning.

marco_eng: I can take the diagram + technical notes. Need to confirm deployment mode: are they asking to run inside their VPC (customer-hosted) or hosted by Redwood in an EU region? That affects subprocessors and whether we can offer BYOK with HSM.

elaine_sales: Customer prefers customer VPC but said they'd accept hosted if we can legally guarantee EU residency for the POC. Also asked whether debug logs / traces could leave the EU during troubleshooting.

marco_eng: TL;DR: For customer-hosted (Private) we can ensure inference data stays in their VPC; control-plane handshakes to Redwood control plane can be restricted to EU endpoints. For Redwood-hosted we store data in EU regions by default, but support/debug metadata may traverse support tooling; we can add contractual support scoping for EU-only processing. I'll include both variants on the diagram.

marco_eng: snippet for diagram: ```
Client (Customer VPC) --[Private Connector]--> Gateway (eu-west1) --> Inference Pool (eu-west1 GPUs)
- Storage: eu-west1 S3 buckets (customer or Redwood-managed)
- KMS: BYOK allowed; we never receive raw keys; key handshake metadata to control-plane endpoint
- Telemetry: disabled by default; debug traces opt-in only and can be restricted to EU by support addendum
```

alyssa_legal: Legal/sec: we can issue an "EU POC Data Residency Statement" conditioned on (i) deployment in eu-west, and (ii) acceptance of our standard POC terms. For Hosted we need the support addendum to promise that debug traces won't leave EU. We can't promise never seeing derived telemetry unless it's contractually scoped. Also: subprocessor export is available but contact-level SOC details require NDA.

mike_se: Pricing: three quick options I'll draft: Hosted POC (no infra setup, pay per usage) — lowest cost; Temporary Dedicated pool (Redwood-managed GPUs reserved) — one-time setup + pro-rated monthly commit; Private (customer infra with private control plane) — higher due to private control-plane license + per-GPU fee. I'll post ballpark numbers once they confirm expected QPS and avg seq length. ETA: EOD today.

elaine_sales: The vendor risk team asked for a redacted subprocessor report (name, role, region, attestations). Can we produce that and include SOC2/SOC3 links?

alyssa_legal: Yes. We have a redacted subprocessor export that omits commercial terms but lists provider name, role (storage/cdn/infra/telemetry), region, and certification links. I'll attach the export and a short note about our 30-day notification policy for new subprocessors. If they ask for contact-level SOC evidence, we'll ask for an NDA.

ops-bot: uploaded: subproc_export_redwood_v2026.pdf (shared to #sales)

marco_eng: One technical caveat for the diagram: cache shards and ephemeral workers may be provisioned regionally. If strict EU-only residency is required, we must pin cache persistence and model shard storage to eu-west and highlight that in the diagram. I'll annotate failure modes (e.g., cross-region fallback disabled).

mike_se: Also flagging BYOK+HSM onboarding: adds time and coordination (legal + ops). Recommend we call out a 10 business day key exchange lead time in the POC proposal.

elaine_sales: Action plan: Marco will drop a one-page PNG/SVG and a pasteable vendor-portal sentence by 09:00 UTC tomorrow; Mike will post three price scenarios today; Alyssa will attach the redacted subproc export + canned legal statements now. I'll follow up with customer to confirm Private vs Hosted.

alyssa_legal: Pasteable statements (two variants):
- Private/Dedicated EU commitment: "For the POC, Redwood will store inference inputs and outputs exclusively in the customer's EU region (eu-west) and will not export debug traces outside the EU unless explicitly authorized in a signed support addendum."
- Hosted EU default: "For the POC, Redwood stores data in EU regions by default; certain control-plane metadata and support traces may be processed outside the EU. Customers can elect the support addendum for EU-only support processing."

elaine_sales: Good. Can you also include a short line about subprocessors notification window?

alyssa_legal: Sure: "Redwood notifies customers at least 30 days before onboarding any new critical subprocessor; customers with enterprise contracts may have custom notification terms."

marco_eng: I'll mark diagram zones that require legal review (KMS handshake wording, subproc contact info). Will upload draft SVG to this thread when ready.

mike_se: Posting a quick price sketch in a follow-up message (will include minimum commit and sample totals).

elaine_sales: Thank you. I'll hold sending the formal vendor portal reply until we have the diagram + subproc export attached.
